_note: EDITORIAL data. The measured half lives in hearing_rates.json and is regenerated by the Legislative Research Tool — never hand-edit rates into this file. Characters are FICTIONAL; the committees, codes, route and deadlines are real. SCOPE: the two MONEY committees only — House Finance and Senate Ways and Means. Every bill with a dollar figure goes through both, they take more referrals than any other committee (876 and 936 in 2026) and they hand back the two lowest hearing rates, so they are where the module's argument lives. Subject-matter committees are deliberately out of scope; if they come back, restore the `singleReferral` roll with them. `championed` is the one place a measured rate is deliberately adjusted: the base covers EVERY measure referred, including the thousands nobody carries, and the player's bills have their introducer working them every week.

hearingGate._note: HARD GATE (2026-10-13, Devin): at this stage the chair will not schedule a bill at all while the campaign influence (plus what you bought for that bill) is under `min`. Probability is 0, not low. A passive campaign sits at 30 and never reaches 28, so the simulator passive anchor is unchanged.

dilution._note: Distinct failure modes: low influence still kills a bill outright (never heard, unchanged). Low SUPPORT does not make the hearing harder — it decides what SURVIVES the hearing: the moment a bill clears a chair gate, support under `floor` takes a bite out of its dollar figure. GRADUATED since 2026-08-21 (it was a cliff at 35, and unreachable besides — per-bill support was written once at seeding and never again, so nothing could ever lower it). `floor` is where dilution starts, `full` is where the per-gate bite reaches its maximum `cut`, and it ramps linearly between the two — so drifting toward the line costs a little before it costs a lot, which is the only version a player can learn from. Multiplicative and stacks across the two money-committee gates (a chronically unpopular bill can limp out of both already thin), floored by `min` so dilution alone never zeroes a bill — killing it stays the job of never-heard/voted-down/conference. floor 45 is deliberately just under the 50 every campaign starts at plus its family tilt: a passive campaign is never diluted (which is what preserves the calibrated bands), but a campaign bleeding support to floor-calendar weeks will be.

familyTilt._note: EDITORIAL, not measured — same standard as `championed`: named, small, a judgment call about who a tax family's natural base is, not survey data. Since 2026-08-21 this is the ONLY per-bill meter data the game stores: a bill's live support/influence are DERIVED as (the campaign's meter + this tilt + whatever the player bought for that bill), never copied and stored. Before that they were absolute numbers seeded once at agenda lock — which happens inside the creation funnel, before any event fx can run, so every campaign's bills started at exactly 50/30 + tilt and then never moved again for the rest of the session. Wealth taxes poll well and lack institutional access; GET is the reverse (broad, visible, unpopular — but the lever leadership reaches for precisely because it avoids concentrated opposition); credits and tourism/admin sit closest to the measured hearing-rate story. Deltas are added to the campaign's meters and clamped 0-100 — they do not touch the measured base rate in baseRate(), which stays untouched by design.

gate._floorMissSupportNote: SUPPORT IS A STOCK AND SOMETHING HAS TO SPEND IT (2026-08-21). The docs have always described support as 'spent at hearings and floor votes'; until now nothing spent it and it only ever went up. A week in which a bill sat on the floor calendar and was not called is that spend — the base turned out for a week that went nowhere. Charged ONCE per week no matter how many bills missed: it is the campaign's week that burned, not each bill's, and a six-bill package would otherwise drop 12 support in a single turn purely for being ambitious.
gate._influenceDecayNote: INFLUENCE IS A RATE, NOT A RATCHET (2026-08-21). Standing inside a building decays when you are not in it, so 'Work the building' is upkeep rather than a one-way climb — which is the distinction between the two meters that the game previously asserted in tooltips and nowhere else. Decays DOWNWARD ONLY, toward `influenceBaseline`, which is the value every campaign starts at: a player knocked below it by events must earn it back and never drifts up for free, and a passive campaign therefore sits exactly at the baseline all session. That is what keeps the simulator's passive band unmoved. It runs during the recess too, deliberately — a week when the Capitol is shut is precisely when a standing slips.

push._note: THE CALL-IN READS BOTH METERS AND COSTS SUPPORT (2026-10-14, Devin). bonus = min(cap, base + max(0, billSupport - supportFrom)/supportDiv + max(0, billInfluence - from)/influenceDiv), and taking it charges `costSupport` off the campaign. WHY IT CHANGED: the old form stepped every `per` points of influence from `from`, so on a wealth bill (-10 influence tilt) the first step needed campaign influence 70 and the push paid a FLAT 0.15 at every meter state a player could actually reach — 'scales with the influence behind it' was true in the code and invisible in play. Continuous now, like every other term in chairOdds: a step nobody reaches teaches nothing, and one they do reach is a cliff they cannot see coming. SUPPORT CARRIES TWO THIRDS OF THE CLIMB because the move is a call-in — the people are the mechanism, the standing is only whether the office picks up. That does NOT repeal 'support must not make a hearing easier unless the chair is aligned': that rule governs support sitting there PASSIVELY, and this is support being SPENT, which is the documented physics of the meter (a stock you spend) finally having something that spends it. STILL ONE-SIDED: `base` IS the old flat 0.15 and the terms only ever ADD, so this can never pay a player less than it used to — the 2026-08-21 lesson about tilted families, unchanged. costSupport 2 IS WHAT MAKES THIS FREE: measured at 12k sessions/cell, push-first lands at 9.65% +/-0.27 against the shipped 9.51% — the same number — while `balanced` gains ~1pp, so the gap over a mixed rotation narrows from 3.2pp to 2.4pp. Passive/rally/bench/lobby never push and are untouched by construction. Full working in PUSH-TWO-METER.md; re-run tools/simulate_gauntlet.py after any edit here.

gate._actionBonusNote: SUPERSEDED by `push` above (2026-08-21); kept because old saves and any un-migrated call site still fall back to it, and because it documents what the flat value used to be.

causes.never heard: The chair never put it on a hearing calendar. No vote was taken, and no record exists of it dying.
causes.voted down: It got a vote and lost.
causes.died in conference: The two chambers could not agree on a final version before the deadline.
causes.ran out of clock: The deadline passed while it was still waiting.

introducers._note: YOUR TWO MEMBERS — the people who actually introduce and carry the bills, because the player never can (The Advocate has no seat and no vote). One per chamber: the House introducer files the package and carries it through Finance and House floor; the Senate introducer picks it up at crossover and carries it through Ways and Means and Senate floor. Which one is 'on point' is derived from the STAGE's chamber (stages.*.chamber), never stored per bill — every bill in module 1 runs the same House-first route, so a per-bill introducer field would be duplicated state that can drift. THE HOUSE INTRODUCER IS REP. CHRISTINA SILVA (renamed from the Rep. X placeholder 2026-10-12, Devin); the Senate one is still the placeholder Sen. X; `char` links to session.json characters exactly the way chairs do, so renaming one means renaming both files. RAPPORT is 0-100 and starts at gate.introBaseline: the odds term is ZERO-CENTRED ((rapport - baseline) / div), so a player who never touches the relationship gets EXACTLY the pre-2026-08-15 numbers and the simulation-calibrated enact-rate bands still hold. Only the swing away from baseline is new. Keep it that way — a rapport term that pays out at baseline would silently re-tune every band in the design doc.
